fix1.shapeTaken: (b), per the dispatch's own recommendation, no reason found not to. IN_SCOPE_CITIES_SQL now GROUP BYs place_fips/city_name/in_city_parcels with array_agg(DISTINCT city_key ORDER BY city_key) AS city_keys, so a multi-layer city is ONE row, not one per layer. HOIST_ZONES_SQL takes city_key = ANY($1::text[]) (was a scalar $1) and now also selects city_key per polygon row into r5_zones_ok. CHUNK_ZONE_MATCH_SQL threads z.city_key through hits/kept/ranked to the final SELECT. processCity hoists city.cityKeys (the full array) once per city and calls buildZoningCells with the MATCHED row's own city_key (m.city_key), never a group-level representative. This also removes the ORDER BY tie hazard structurally: there is exactly one processCity pass per place_fips now, never two racing over which throws first.
fix1.correctnessGapFoundBeyondTheDispatch: The dispatch's own text asks only to confirm sourceUrl survives a union pass ('buildZoningCells already records sourceUrl per matched parcel from whichever zone row matched'). Reading the caller showed a SECOND cell, zoningJurisdictionKey, was being written from city.cityKey -- the single row-level key of a single-layer city -- which a naive union implementation (keep writing one group-level key for every match) would silently mislabel for any parcel matched via the OTHER layer in the union. This is exactly the class of silent mislabeling this program's own DEV_PROCESS section 2 exists to catch. Fixed by making zoningJurisdictionKey, like sourceUrl, travel from the matched row, not the group.
fix1.sourceUrlAndJurisdictionKeyProvenanceCon: Live, 2026-09-09, real production data, not a fixture: a matched Bastrop parcel (103412) carries source_url .../Elgin_Zoning/FeatureServer/0 and city_key=elgin-tx. Separately, the union pass produced 411 CROSS-BOUNDARY matches (409 Bastrop-county parcels matched via the elgin-tx-travis/FeatureServer-1 polygon, 2 Travis-county parcels matched via the elgin-tx/FeatureServer-0 polygon) -- confirmed each carries the CORRECT per-match city_key and source_url for the layer it actually matched (e.g. Travis parcels 557529 and 965082 both carry city_key=elgin-tx, source_url=.../FeatureServer/0, correctly naming the Bastrop-side layer that actually covers them despite being Travis-county parcels). A naive group-level fallback would have written elgin-tx-travis for all 409 Bastrop cross-matches and elgin-tx for neither of the 2 Travis ones (or the reverse), which is the exact defect class the new unit test (a synthetic two-layer fixture) pins directly.

Whether those ~21 cities' actual (different, unidentified) staging mechanism has some OTHER, structurally different filtering step with an analogous risk is UNRUN, not claimed clear -- that would require finding and auditing whatever DID stage them, which this dispatch's hauska-factory-only, no-hauska-engine-write scope did not include and this lane did not attempt.

proposedCeiling_NOT_written.derivation: 9 = the original CTX-ELGIN figure, independently re-confirmed unchanged today (same 9 prop_ids, still zero live polygon coverage under the rail's own union-based measurement, which did not move Bastrop's matched count at all). 456 = 506 (this lane's live union measurement) minus 50 (the freshly-found Travis staleness class) minus 0 (S-P), with the 456 remainder independently re-confirmed via a second, different predicate (point-in-polygon, not overlap-with-floor) and a working positive control -- NOT simply asserted from the arithmetic.
proposedCeiling_NOT_written.whyNoCeilingIsActuallyReadyToWrite_theLo: assertResidueWithinDeclaration compares the FULL RAW per-county residue (36, 506 -- every residual parcel of a declared-layer-gap CITY, with no per-PARCEL distinction) against whatever ceiling is declared. buildLayerGapCells is gated the same way: isDeclaredLayerGap(cityName) is a per-CITY boolean, so EVERY residual parcel of Elgin -- staleness, S-P, or genuinely uncovered alike -- is written as a 'refused' cell candidate once apply=true runs, subject only to the gated UPDATE's 'currently unaccounted' clause. Checked live (read-only, FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO, SELECT only) against the ACTUAL current parcel_record_cell state: all 17 Bastrop staleness parcels and all 50 Travis staleness parcels are STILL 'unaccounted' today (the Factory re-bake CTX-ELGIN's close said was needed has not happened). The 10 Bastrop S-P parcels are already 'value' (their write would be an inert no-op today, but only by accident of already having resolved some other way -- not because the mechanism protects them). This means: any ceiling >= 36/506 (large enough to let the rail actually write) would ALSO authorize sweeping the 17+50 STILL-unaccounted staleness parcels to 'refused' -- permanently relabeling 'we have not looked' as 'we looked and there is no answer', for parcels that in fact already have a resolvable answer sitting in txgio_parcel, one re-bake away. This is precisely the relabelling tripwire named in _decisions/2026-09-08_zoning_unaccounted_two_populations.md ('watch for an unaccounted count falling without an acquisition landing... that is relabelling') -- a more specific instance of it than that decision's own text anticipated (it named the not-applicable/unwired-city split; this lane found the SAME risk one level down, inside the refused/layer-gap sweep itself). A ceiling of 9/456 (the genuinely-uncovered-only figures) would NOT clear the guard at all, since the guard compares against the raw 36/506, not a staleness-and-S-P-excluded subset -- the code has no mechanism to express that exclusion today. THEREFORE: no ceiling number, of any size, is currently safe to propose as ready. The fix this exposes is a CODE change (scoping buildLayerGapCells's write-eligibility, and assertResidueWithinDeclaration's counted population, to an explicit per-parcel allowlist rather than a per-city boolean) -- squarely beyond this dry-run-only lane's mandate and a genuinely new, separate finding from Fix 1's scoping defect.
proposedCeiling_NOT_written.recommendedFollowOn: A short, separately-dispatched hauska-factory lane to make the layer-gap population per-parcel rather than per-city: DECLARED_LAYER_GAP should carry an explicit list (or a derivable rule) of WHICH residual parcels are refused-eligible, excluding any parcel that (a) already carries a real value in txgio_parcel pending only a re-bake, or (b) is geometrically covered by a known-but-unmapped district code. Only once that exists does '9 Bastrop / 456 Travis' become a number the code can actually enforce correctly; until then, writing either 9/456 or 36/506 into config repeats a version of the exact error this whole dispatch chain exists to stop.

leave_behind.text: 2026-09-09, live, post-Fix-1: Elgin's group residue is 36 Bastrop (48021) / 506 Travis (48453), against declared ceilings of 9/457. Decomposition -- Bastrop: 9 confirmed genuine gap (unchanged from CTX-ELGIN, re-verified live) + 17 staleness (still 'unaccounted' in parcel_record_cell today, needs a Factory re-bake, NOT a refused sweep) + 10 S-P-covered (already 'value' in parcel_record_cell, covered by a real live S-P district hauska-engine's registry does not map). Travis: 50 staleness (also still 'unaccounted' today) + 0 S-P + 456 independently-confirmed genuine gap.

2026-09-09, live: the 11 S-P polygons on Elgin_Zoning FeatureServer/0 cover exactly the same 10 Bastrop prop_ids CTX-ELGIN found on 2026-09-09 (12948, 111348, 14457, 124619, 12830, 8712013, 60891, 11364, 85259, 14535) and zero Travis residue parcels.

2026-09-09, live: 411 parcels match a layer whose conventional 'home county' differs from the parcel's own county (409 Bastrop parcels matched via elgin-tx-travis, 2 Travis parcels matched via elgin-tx). The two ArcGIS FeatureServer layers geographically overlap across the county line substantially, not cleanly partitioned by county as prior closes' 'Bastrop-side/Travis-side' shorthand implied.

A per-city boolean gate (isDeclaredLayerGap / assertResidueWithinDeclaration) cannot express 'sweep only these specific parcels as refused' -- it is all-or-nothing at the city level. When a declared-gap population turns out, on individual validation, to contain a subset that should NOT be refused (here: parcels with a pending real value one re-bake away, and parcels covered by a real-but-unmapped district), the per-city gate has no way to exclude just that subset. Before proposing ANY numeric ceiling for a per-city gate, check whether the population it would authorize is actually homogeneous -- a validated count is not the same thing as a safe-to-authorize population.

Two ArcGIS FeatureServer layers labeled 'county A side' and 'county B side' for a city split across a county line are not a reliable proxy for a clean geographic partition -- a city's zoning district polygons are drawn to the CITY limit, not the county line, so large districts near the boundary routinely straddle it in the raw published data regardless of which ArcGIS layer index they were published under. A fix that unions such layers (per-parcel best-overlap match) will find real matches an isolated per-layer test structurally cannot, and the resulting residue count can differ from an isolated-layer measurement even when nothing else changed -- reconcile that difference by tracing specific cross-boundary matches, not by assuming the isolated test was authoritative.

The Factory re-bake that would move the 17 Bastrop + 50 Travis staleness parcels from parcel_record_cell 'unaccounted' to 'value' (reading the already-current txgio_parcel state) has not run since CTX-ELGIN's 2026-08 close first identified this need. Recommend the integration seat trigger it BEFORE any layer-gap sweep runs for Elgin, since running the sweep first (even at a large enough ceiling) would foreclose the correct resolution for those 67 parcels.

The per-parcel-eligibility code change this close's proposedCeiling section names (scoping DECLARED_LAYER_GAP / buildLayerGapCells / assertResidueWithinDeclaration to an explicit per-parcel allowlist rather than a per-city boolean) is real, scoped, evidence-backed follow-on work this lane identified but is not authorized to apply (a mechanism change, not a config edit, and beyond a dry-run-only mandate). Recommend a short, separately-dispatched lane.

Whether the ~21 non-registry-governed declared-complete cities' actual staging mechanism (unidentified by this lane; not packages/engine-core/src/zoning-staging/registry.ts, which only covers elgin-tx and smithville-tx) has some structurally different code-filtering step with a defect class analogous to Elgin's S-P exclusion is UNRUN. This lane conclusively ruled out THIS SPECIFIC mechanism for those cities (they are not registry entries at all) but did not locate or audit whatever mechanism actually staged them -- that would require reading further into hauska-engine or wherever that pipeline lives, out of this dispatch's scope.

This close's Travis validation could not cross-check against CTX-ELGIN's/CTX-STAGE2's original exact 457 parcel list because no artifact in doc_repo _inbox persists it (only the count, unlike Bastrop's exact 9). Recommend future closes that establish a per-county confirmed-gap ceiling always persist the exact parcel ID list, not just the count, precisely so a later lane's delta validation does not have to re-derive the whole population from scratch, as this one did.
